probe_type: deterministic symbolic recurrence cut with two resume arms
tested_scope: Serialized single-writer role-local conditional updates; one predecessor pointer P20; one durable intent I21 with a fresh attempt nonce and deterministic semantic operation digest; one native effect E21 already applied exactly once; one valid certificate C21 written successfully but its response lost before pointer CAS; deterministic native-effect identity and exact equality checks are available on restart.

initial_durable_cut.lost_response_cut: C21 create succeeded durably; caller did not receive the success response; P20->C21 CAS was never attempted.

algorithm: Read P20 and treat absence of pointer advancement as absence of the transition.
Create a fresh retry attempt for the same semantic operation.
Apply the semantic native effect again.
Write a replacement epoch-21 certificate and CAS P20 to it.
arm_naive_pointer_only_retry.verdict: FAIL: pointer-only restart cannot distinguish a lost successful certificate response from a never-started transition, so retry duplicates the already-applied semantic native effect.

algorithm: Read P20 and the durable pending intent I21 instead of inferring completion solely from P20.

Fetch the exact certificate slot bound to I21 and require exact equality: C21.epoch=P20.epoch+1, C21.predecessor_certificate=P20.certificate, C21.intent_id=I21, C21.attempt_nonce=I21.attempt_nonce, and C21.effect_id=I21.effect_id.
Require native evidence E21 to exist exactly once and require E21.effect_digest=C21.effect_digest.
Because the exact certificate and native effect already match, do not replay E21.
Conditionally repair only the pointer with CAS(expected=P20, new=C21), then reread P and E21.
arm_intent_bound_idempotent_resume.verdict: PASS within tested scope: a durable intent plus exact certificate/native-effect equality turns the ambiguous lost-response cut into a pointer-only repair, preserving the already-completed semantic effect exactly once.

mechanism_revision: Generation+nonce+certificate-first pointer repair is insufficient if restart has no durable way to rediscover the exact in-flight certificate after an ambiguous successful write. Add a durable intent identity before the native effect, bind certificate and deterministic native-effect identity to that intent, and on restart prefer exact intent/certificate/native equality plus pointer-only CAS over replay.
scope_guard: This does not prove safety when the native effect itself has an ambiguous response before certificate creation, when E_native lacks a queryable deterministic identity, under concurrent writers, under certificate/native corruption, under malicious mutation, or when repository transport violates the assumed serialized conditional-update model.

mechanism_assessment.repository_transport_role: Only bounded role-local persistence/readback and conditional pointer transport; no hosted compute, runner, Codespaces, artifact/LFS/package service, external model/API credit, or repository API volume used as computation.
mechanism_assessment.accepted_scope: Ambiguous successful certificate-write response after a native effect already has exact durable identity, before pointer CAS, under serialized single-writer recurrence.

conflict_check: Semantic inputs were restricted to frozen sanitized root/control, current neuroscience role config, and own neuroscience LATEST/preflight. No O, other-worker, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger, other-role receipt/config, scheduler, or unrelated repository semantics were used.
exact_next_action: On the next valid invocation, execute exactly one earlier-cut ambiguous-native-effect probe: simulate E_native succeeding while its response is lost before C21 exists. Compare a queryable deterministic effect-id resume rule against a replay rule; require exactly-once semantic effect without assuming certificate existence. If E_native cannot expose durable idempotency/query semantics, record that exact missing Chat-native capability as an unresolved child rather than promoting this mechanism beyond the current cut.
